fatal_errors: The proposed Mo-coated W-particle intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated liquid-metal dealloying of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu.

None of the cited evidence supports Mo interlayers reducing W/Cu thermal boundary resistance or preserving W–Cu irradiation resistance; the citations concern WC–HEA mechanical properties, generic HEA-reinforced matrices, and irradiation behavior of a different refractory HEA.
Mechanical durability and irradiation resistance of the proposed Mo-coated composite are asserted without relevant evidence or a defined irradiation regime.
The conditions are too vague to establish applicability: coating thickness, consolidation method, temperature range, irradiation species, energy, fluence, and damage level are unspecified.
explanation: The hypothesis is aligned with the broad W–Cu heat-management and fusion-joint objective and supplies a control-based experiment, but it is scientifically disconnected from the hidden target. The target uses 1200 °C, 96 h liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor to generate aligned Cu channels, continuous refractory-HEA ligaments, and a spontaneous W-rich interlayer. Its thermal and irradiation claims are bounded to measured temperature-dependent conductivity and low-energy He+ screening of precursor dendrites. The generated response instead proposes an unsupported Mo coating and invokes generic phonon bridging, neutron or ion irradiation, and retained mechanical performance without directly relevant citations. Its experiment could test the alternative in principle, but lacks quantitative processing and exposure conditions and uses a compound falsification rule that may obscure a conductivity benefit accompanied by durability loss.
